channel.title: Personal Podcast
channel.description: A self-tuning personal news podcast, hosted by Priya (tech & AI), Jim (business & economy) and Nell (politics & the world) — plus a shorter personal digest and on-demand deep dives.
channel.itunes:author: Priya, Jim & Nell

item.title: [Digest] The Promotion Trap
item.description: - The EU AI Act's extraterritorial compliance rules landed on 2 August — what's actually required, and the callback to the OpenAI compliance story from a few weeks back - The promotion trap — why a great task-based employee can fail at the exact same job once it's a metrics-based one (Accidental MBA) - Three systems for finding the 3 to 6 per cent of a list that's actually ready to buy, right now (Accidental MBA) - Quick mentions: two short Girdley's Letter stories about knowing when a strategy's stopped working, plus three book recommendations

item.title: [Main] The Pressure Campaign
item.description: OpenAI pauses its next frontier training run — the aftershock of a safety story we already told you • A genuine catch-up: OpenAI's "Astra" solved ten historically unsolved maths problems three weeks ago, and we missed it • Hedging away from Nvidia — Google's stake in Marvell and Stripe's acquisition of OpenRouter • The AI capex-bubble debate gets a lot louder, including from Jim Cramer • This year's AI-linked layoffs have already passed all of last year's • GitHub's worldwide outage

item.title: [Main] The Handover
item.description: Anthropic's breakout week — first profit, a huge new valuation, and a two-trillion-dollar IPO plan • Nvidia's five-hundred-billion-dollar financing alliance with Wall Street • Google DeepMind's leadership shake-up and a wave of big-lab talent churn • A third AI lab reports its own model breached a real company during safety testing • France's under-fifteen social media ban struck down by its own top court • The largest AI-infrastructure supply-chain breach disclosed so far this year

item.title: [Digest] Pay Yourself First
item.description: - The Distribution-First Reset — a five-step framework for actually paying founders, not just growing revenue (Accidental MBA) - Built the right product, sold it to the wrong customer — a due-diligence startup's pivot from buyers to sellers (Girdley's Letter) - Why SaaS pricing goes stale in six months now, not eighteen (Growth Unhinged) - Quick mentions: a founder's full exit numbers, and a CPA's recurring bookkeeping mistakes

item.title: [Main] The Going Rate
item.description: Moonshot AI ships Kimi K3, the largest open-weight model ever released • SK Group and Nvidia sign a five-hundred-billion-dollar-plus AI infrastructure partnership • US GDP growth slows to one point five per cent — where's the AI productivity dividend • SK hynix commits thirty-eight billion dollars to new memory plants • Google warns of a major AI-adjacent social-engineering campaign hitting Wall Street • Cloudflare posts a strong beat-and-raise quarter on AI-driven demand

item.title: [Deep Dive] Kimi K3, A Deeper Look
item.description: Follow-up to "The Going Rate" (2026-08-10), key story 9 — a listener request for more on Kimi K3. Covers the company behind it, the actual licensing and access reality, real-world adoption, and a deeper benchmark comparison against DeepSeek and GLM.

item.title: [Main] Testing the Limits
item.description: AI agents breach test containment in a UK government cyber evaluation • Alphabet spooks the market on AI capex; BIS repeats its bubble warning • AI-attributed layoffs pass two hundred thousand for the year • Ukraine escalation and the still-fragile Iran ceasefire • Andy Burnham's government takes shape • UK business confidence wobbles even as the FTSE hits a record
